data.name: Mihraz
data.long_meaning: In Islamic architecture, the Mihrab is a niche in the wall of a mosque indicating the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca. The person who ensures the Mihrab is clean and well-maintained is known as Mihraz.
data.spiritual_meaning: A guardian of spiritual direction and guidance.

data.cultural_impact: The Mihrab, as a physical structure, marks and symbolizes the unity of Muslims towards the holiest site in Islam, the Kaaba in Mecca. It denotes the common direction of the Muslim community in prayers towards Mecca, emphasizing their shared faith and spiritual connection.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mihraz holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the spiritual anchor guiding Muslims to the House of Allah (Kaaba). It underlines the importance of unwavering faith, commitment and unity with fellow believers, enabling each one to focus their prayers towards Allah and seek His blessings.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd, Kitab Al-Tabaqat Al-Kabir, Volume 2, Page 165. The name Mihraz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mihraz was the name of a building in Mecca where the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) used to perform the Tawaf (pilgrimage around the Kaaba) before the construction of the Masjid al-Haram (Great Mosque) in Mecca.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab Al-Ashraf, Volume 1, Page 377. The name Mihraz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mihraz was also the name of a structure in the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, where the Imam led the congregational prayers. It was located near the Prophet's pulpit and was used as a place for the Imam to ascend the pulpit (minbar) during his sermons.
